teaser: What never scaled is on-demand expertise: the before and after the meeting. Agents can now carry them, for any expert, anywhere.
core_idea: Many old jobs never scaled because on-demand expertise depended on weeks of context gathering before the meeting and writing up after it, which experts dislike and are not hired for; agents can now carry both phases, as the clinic's support staff do for a specialist, so historians, librarians, consultants and others can work for any project, anywhere, even part-time, and service businesses can grow with judgement rather than hours.

quotes.text: What is a consultant? Somebody who has skills the team does not have.
That is part of their magic: what questions to ask.
The specialist is not effective because they work less.
But agents can go in all directions, and you need somebody who provides the direction.

figures.caption: Before, the meeting, after. Then: a week or more gathering, a day or two meeting, three days or more writing up, about three weeks for one engagement. Now: agents gather and write up, and the expert's time goes on the meeting and the decisions.
The clinic model. First, others collect your history; then the specialist reads the key facts and decides; last, a team carries out the plan. Agents can be that first and last group for any expert.

The intersection that made outside expertise rare: a company with the problem, someone who had hired the right talent, someone who could travel there, and a budget big enough. Now the expert can be anywhere, and the context and the delivery travel to and from them.

Twelve jobs that never scaled: historian, librarian, cartographer, architect, on-demand consultant, lawyer reviewing a contract, accountant, doctor and specialist, sherpa, security lead, project manager, translator.
Twelve good hours, illustrative. Without support, a part-time expert's week goes mostly on gathering and writing up. With agents carrying those, nearly all of it goes on judgement and meetings.
